== Race summary ==

=== Special elections during the preceding Congress ===
Special U.S. Senate elections in Florida and Ohio are scheduled for November 3, 2026. Florida voters will elect a candidate to serve the remaining two years of former Senator [[Marco Rubio]]'s unexpired term;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bgov.com/bloomberg-government-news/new-florida-senator-moody-faces-first-election-test-in-2026|title=New Florida Senator Moody Faces First Election Test in 2026|website=bgov.com|last=Giroux|first=Greg|date=January 17, 2025}}</ref> Rubio resigned his seat in 2025 to become [[United States Secretary of State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beggin |first=Riley |title=Trump taps Marco Rubio for Secretary of State |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2024/11/13/trump-marco-rubio-secretary-state/76198371007/ |website=[[USA Today]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Ohio voters will elect a candidate to serve the remaining two years of former Senator [[JD Vance]]'s unexpired term; Vance resigned in 2025 to become [[2024 United States presidential election|Vice President of the United States]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/senate-ohio-governor-dewine-vance-5dc31a64a23a798dd7e6915783e7a395|title=Ohio Lt. Gov. Jon Husted will succeed JD Vance in the US Senate|first1=Julie Carr|last1=Smyth|first2=Stephen|last2=Groves|date=January 17, 2025|publisher=Associated Press}}</ref>

Elections are sorted by date then state.
